terms.comment: Intransitive fermentation can be expressed with the passive fermentārī.
Ancient, attested in Pliny, not merely a later invention.

terms.gloss: swell up, rise: of a cake in the oven
evidence: Col. 1.4.10: locō tamen ipsō paululum intumēscente (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to swell up; to rise”, of waves and of the ground. Of a cake rising in the oven its use is ours; fermentārī is said of dough rising with leaven.

phrases.latin: tulit igitur populus cōnspersam farīnam antequam fermentārētur
phrases.english: so the people took their dough before it was leavened

phrases.latin: fīcus … in dōleum vel in amphorās conditur et ibi sinitur fermentārī
phrases.english: the figs are put into a jar or into amphorae and there left to ferment

phrases.latin: Sine fermentētur; post hōram in furnum mittēmus.
phrases.english: Let it rise; in an hour we’ll put it in the oven.

phrases.latin: Jamne fermentāta est? — Nōndum; exspectēmus paulisper.
phrases.english: Has it risen yet? — Not yet; let’s wait a little.
Look, the cake has risen in the oven!

sources: Lewis & Short: fermento · Lewis & Short: fermentesco · Lewis & Short: intumesco
